handling. We realized that one of the common causes of varying performance was basically memory pressure, and a lot of the memory pressure comes actually from AL code doing things requiring a lot of memory.
So what we have introduced in this release, and the work is ongoing, is we've created a new platform code unit for dealing with base 64 conversion.

Because for OData returns, they are converted into strings using base 64 convert. So there is a new platform code unit, and then we have modified the existing code units to make use of this new platform code unit,
and also introduced a method which allows you to put the result of this into a stream, also reducing the memory pressure from this operation.
The new platform code unit has a significantly lower memory footprint than the older implementation. What this means to you
is actually very simple. You don't need to change any code. What you'll see is fewer out of memory exceptions, but also AL errors where we have caught the excessive memory usage.
So you basically need to react to those and put limits in. We cannot generate arbitrarily large base 64 strings.
If you try to do something on a 15 GB document, you will now see these new errors. So overall, you see an improved performance,
and particularly if you make use of the new stream overloads. And I probably also, if your friends are using this, the performance of the your environments will go up Yes.
